traits.ribs.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Lophophora: stems usually gray-green or blue-green to dark green, usually flat-topped and cryptic in the soil surface, sometimes protruding above it with a recessed apex, ribbed or weakly tuberculate, 2-7.5 × (4-)5-12 cm, softly fleshy, dull, glabrous; ribs 5, 8 or 13 (rarely 21), low, broadly rounded, straight; areoles 3-15+ mm apart along the ribs or at the apices of low, humplike tubercles, copiously hairy, the hairs in compact erect tufts to 7-10 mm. Spines absent. Flowers deeply nestled in the areolar hairs at the stem apex, campanulate, 1-3 × (1-)1.5-2.5 cm; ovary smooth, scales, hairs and spines absent. Fruits white to pinkish, clavate to nearly cylindric, 11-25 × (2-)4-5 mm, spines and scales absent. Its blue-green by hand.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), : Lophophora: outer tepals whitish to greenish pink, midrib greenish; inner tepals usually white to pink, 8-14(-22) × (1-)2.5-5 mm; stigma lobes (3-)4-8, white or pinkish. Lophophora williamsii: plants 0-50-branched, nearly flush with the soil surface; stems flat or domelike with a deeply depressed centre; ribs to 25 mm broad. Inner tepals elliptic, margins white to greenish pink, midstripes darker; styles white. Flowering Mar-May(-Sep). The carpels are as many as the stigma lobes; colours by hand from the words.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from the flora's words: a few soft, flat-topped heads sunk to their rims, clumping with age, a pale pink flower or two in the wool at the centre of each. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: A rough stem height, most of it below ground: about 6 cm by 25 years. Wide tolerance.

appearance.note: Rib depth and sharpness by eye for the flora's 'low, broadly rounded' ribs; the tufts' size from its 'compact erect tufts to 7-10 mm', their colour (not in the flora) a pale cream by eye.

taxon.note: Scientific names as WCVP v16 accepts them, common names as the Flora of North America gives them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).
